headline: KSE-100 sheds 2,547 points (-1.41%) to 177,955.51 as fading US-Iran ceasefire hopes and a fresh Imran Khan hospital-transfer order trigger broad, indiscriminate selling — even the oil beneficiaries got caught.
summary: PSX had a rough session: the KSE-100 dropped 2,547 points (-1.41%) to close at 177,955.51. Two shocks combined — fading hopes for a renewed US-Iran ceasefire pushed oil toward three-week highs, raising Strait of Hormuz shipping fears and Pakistan's oil-import-bill worries, while the Supreme Court's order moving Imran Khan to hospital added fresh political uncertainty. Selling was broad and indiscriminate: even OGDC and Mari Energies, the sector meant to benefit from pricier oil, got sold off alongside banks, cement and fertilizers. Global markets stayed calm by comparison, so this reads as a Pakistan-specific risk-off day, not a global one. The desk's lean: stay selective, favour names with a real, dated reason to move, not a broad sector story.

sectors.name: E&P (OGDC/PPL/MARI)
sectors.why: Structurally the clear beneficiary of a Hormuz-driven oil-price premium, but today's tape shows even OGDC and Mari Energies were sold off with everything else — the thesis is intact, patience and sizing discipline matter more than chasing it today.

sectors.name: Banks
sectors.why: Genuinely mixed picture: fixed-income/carry-book earnings still get support from T-bill yields (11.7%) sitting well above the held 11.5% policy rate, but UBL — a fundamentally attractive name — was today's single biggest index drag, and the desk caps new cyclical bank exposure in a risk-off regime.

sectors.name: Cement
sectors.why: Energy- and import-cost heavy, and named among today's broad-based sell-off sectors, despite a genuinely strong July dispatch data print (+17.3% YoY) earlier this week.

sectors.name: OMCs & Refineries
sectors.why: Hormuz-adjacent shipping disruption and elevated crude are a physical supply-security and margin risk right now, not just a price optic.

sectors.name: Autos
sectors.why: Import- and energy-cost intensive, and directly exposed to a sustained oil-price and PKR shock — one of today's weaker sectors.

sectors.name: Textiles & exporters
sectors.why: FY26 current account just flipped to a marginal $139mn deficit after a $1.84bn FY25 surplus on an import surge; a sustained oil shock compounds that pressure.

watchlist.angle: The desk's strongest signal today: a live obv_divergence_up trigger (volume leads price) that has won 96.6% of the time across 89 backtested trades and still 83% out-of-sample — the highest-confidence active signal on the board. It lines up with attractive fundamentals (P/E near 6.5, a 32% net margin) and fresh news: a Rs10bn sponsor capital injection into the bank was approved today, though the mechanism and timeline aren't disclosed yet.
watchlist.risk: Banks are broadly on the macro desk's avoid list in this risk-off regime outside the carry-book angle, and the capital-injection terms are still unconfirmed — a weak structure or delay would undercut the news catalyst.

watchlist.angle: A live trend_momo_combo signal fired today (medium confidence, 66.7% out-of-sample hit rate over 37 trades), and the stock screens cheap on the numbers — P/E near 5.5 with a healthy 12.5% net margin.
watchlist.risk: Automobile assemblers are explicitly on the macro desk's avoid list right now — import- and energy-cost heavy, exactly what a Hormuz-driven oil shock threatens. This technical trigger is fighting the macro backdrop, not riding it.

watchlist.angle: No live technical trigger, but two real threads line up: a confirmed book-closure and dividend date on 2026-08-22 (Rs1.5/share), and improving fundamentals — forward P/E of 6.4 versus a trailing 8.7 — on the heels of an already-reported record FY26 profit.
watchlist.risk: Cement sits on the macro desk's avoid list this cycle, and today's broad selloff hit cement stocks alongside everything else — the dividend date is real, but so is the sector headwind.

watchlist.angle: One of the stronger-rated banks on the board — P/E near 8.7 with a covered 8.6% dividend yield — carrying a confirmed book-closure date tomorrow, 2026-08-19 (Rs9.0/share). It also fits the one bank exception the macro desk allows in this regime: strong fixed-income/carry-book earnings support while T-bill yields (11.7%) stay well above the policy rate.
watchlist.risk: Banks broadly remain capped in a risk-off regime, and today proved sector-quality doesn't guarantee protection — UBL, a similarly well-rated bank, was the single biggest drag on the index.

catalysts.event: MCB book closure (dividend Rs9.0/share, 2.21% yield); also the next SBP T-bill (MTB) auction results are due
SBP weekly FX reserves print — watched for whether the recovery streak extends
MSCI Frontier Market Small Cap Index reconstitution effective date — AIRLINK added, Biafo Industries removed
SBP Monetary Policy Committee decision, now shadowed by the Middle East oil-price risk to the further-cuts outlook
Next Supreme Court hearing on Imran Khan's health/access petitions — ongoing domestic political overhang

risks: Middle East escalation: the US-Iran ceasefire deadline expired 2026-08-17 without a deal; a further Strait of Hormuz disruption would widen Pakistan's import bill and pressure the rupee further.
Domestic political overhang: the Supreme Court's Imran Khan hospital-transfer order keeps a live uncertainty item on the calendar into the 2026-09-16 hearing.

PKR and import-bill pressure: FY26's current account just flipped to a $139mn deficit after a $1.84bn FY25 surplus — a sustained oil-price shock widens that gap and keeps the SBP cautious into the 2026-09-14 rate decision.
